record.what_it_does: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) for sending and receiving business messages, templates and calls.
record.auth_notes: Graph API calls use Bearer access tokens. There are three ways to get one. A temporary token from the API Setup page expires quickly. A permanent System User token is created in Business Settings with the whatsapp_business_messaging, whatsapp_business_management and business_management permissions. Embedded Signup, which uses Facebook Login for Business, lets each end-customer business connect its own WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) and get a token. A multi-user toolkit would use Embedded Signup/Facebook Login for Business OAuth, with a system user token for server-side calls. I did not read the access-tokens page itself, because the fetch returned only navigation text.
record.access_notes: A developer can create a Meta app and use the API Setup flow with a temporary token, and this is free. I could not confirm the free test number or the pricing from the pages I fetched, because they returned only navigation text. Serving other businesses needs Meta App Review (advanced access to the whatsapp_business_* permissions), Business Verification, and Tech Provider onboarding for Embedded Signup. Messaging is billed per message by Meta on a pay-as-you-go basis, with a Pricing page in the docs. Tech Provider and Embedded Signup details are from the docs index, not from pages I read.
record.api_breadth_notes: This is the Graph API (REST-style) under graph.facebook.com. It covers sending messages (text, media, templates, interactive), media, phone numbers, message templates, business profile, calling, groups, flows, payments and WABA management. I did not count operations. GraphQL is Graph API generic and not the main surface, so the styles list is a guess.
record.mcp_notes: Meta announced an official "WhatsApp Business Tools MCP" in a developer blog post dated 2026-09-15. The setup guide is reported at developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp/whatsapp-business-tools-mcp, which I did not open. It is added to Claude, Codex or ChatGPT and signs in with Facebook Login for Business. It is for development and testing, not high-volume sending. I did not see the server URL. Several community servers also exist.
record.blocker_notes: Building and testing is self-serve. Letting arbitrary end-users connect their own WABAs needs Meta App Review, Business Verification and Tech Provider onboarding for Embedded Signup. Messaging is also paid per message, and template rules and the 24-hour customer service window constrain agent behavior.
